name: Z-spider special rule
summary: Copying a wire with a Z-spider and merging it back again gives the identity.
description:
Two phase-free Z-spiders connected by two parallel wires, each with one other leg, equal a plain wire. In terms of Frobenius algebras this says that the Z-spider is *special*. Classically: copying a bit and then comparing the two copies does nothing.

In the ZX-calculus this follows from [spider fusion](../spider-fusion/), [self-loop removal](../self-loop-removal/) and [identity removal](../identity-removal/). In the ZH-calculus it is one of the axioms; the phase-free (ZS2) of the original paper also states that the arity-2 Z-spider is the identity.
